articles.summary: Finance Company Financial Management in Nigeria: A Practical Guide for Growing Businesses Oluwakemi Adesina September 28, 2026 A company can make more sales and still struggle to pay its bills on time. This is where company financial management in Nigeria becomes important. Money owed to your business is not the same as money sitting in your bank account. You need to know what is coming in, what is going out, and what your business can actually afford. Good financial management helps you stay in control of your money while planning for expenses, changes in costs, and future growth. What Is Company Financial Management in Nigeria? Company financial management is simply how a business plans and manages its money. It involves knowing how much is coming in, what the business needs to spend, and what should be kept aside for future expenses. The goal is to make sure the money available to the business is being used wisely and that there is enough to cover important expenses as they come up. It is also different from bookkeeping. Bookkeeping tells you what has already happened, such as an invoice raised, a salary paid, or fuel purchased. Financial management helps you use that information to decide what to do next. For example, can the business afford to hire another person? Can you take on a new supplier with the current payment terms? Will there be enough cash to cover expenses if sales slow down next month? Good records tell you where your business has been. Good financial management helps you decide where it can go next. Why Financial Management Matters for Nigerian Businesses Good financial management gives a business owner a clear picture of what is happening with the company’s money. It helps you know what you can afford, what needs to wait, and which decisions are backed by actual numbers. Take a boutique fashion business in Lagos. Its order book is full, and its accountant says the business made a profit last quarter. But customers pay 45 to 60 days after delivery, fabric suppliers require payment upfront, and staff still need to be paid at the end of the month. The business may be profitable on paper, but its cash could still be stretched. This is where financial management matters. It helps a business plan expenses around when cash will actually come in, manage working capital, prepare for payroll, and identify unnecessary costs. Cash Flow Management for Companies Cash flow is the money moving in and out of a business within a given period. A company can be profitable and still run out of cash to operate, as happened to the boutique label above. Common Cash Flow Challenges Cash flow problems often come from a few familiar issues: customers paying late, operating costs slowly increasing, buying too much inventory too early, or having a large payroll due before enough customer payments come in. An unexpected expense can also put pressure on cash, especially when there is no clear plan for when money will come in and when bills need to be paid. How Businesses Can Improve Cash Flow Start with a simple cash flow forecast. Even a basic spreadsheet can help you see when money is expected to come in and when major expenses are due. Keep track of customers who owe you money and how long their payments have been outstanding. Review your payment dates and expenses regularly, and cut costs that are no longer adding value to the business. It is also worth setting aside some cash for unexpected expenses or a slower month. There will be one. Having a reserve gives the business room to handle it without disrupting payroll or other important payments. Business Budgeting and Financial Planning A working budget starts with an honest revenue forecast. Look at what is actually selling, existing contracts, seasonal changes such as the Q4 rush or January slowdown, and how quickly customers usually pay. Do not build the budget around when you hope the money will arrive. Then account for the costs of running the business. This includes payroll, rent, utilities, marketing, software subscriptions, inventory, professional services such as audit and legal fees, and the smaller expenses that can add up quickly. Payroll is often one of the biggest and least flexible costs, which is why it deserves closer attention. But creating the budget is only the beginning. Check it against what is actually happening each month. If spending is higher than expected or revenue falls short, find out why and adjust early. Small gaps are much easier to deal with before they become bigger problems. Managing Payroll as Part of Company Financial Management Payroll is more than an HR expense. For many businesses, it is one of the largest recurring costs, and it has to be paid on a fixed date whether or not customers have paid their invoices. That makes payroll one of the clearest tests of how well a company is managing its finances. Getting payroll right starts with planning salaries around actual cash flow, not expected payments. It also means applying deductions correctly and keeping statutory contributions up to date. For employers, this includes PAYE, pension contributions, and other applicable statutory deductions. The Nigeria Tax Act 2025 introduced changes to personal income tax from 1 January 2026, so businesses need to make sure their payroll calculations reflect the current rules. Under the contributory pension scheme, the minimum contribution is 18% of monthly emoluments, with 10% paid by the employer and 8% deducted from the employee. The important point is that these costs need to be included in the financial plan. Salaries and statutory payments should not come as a surprise at the end of the month. They should already be accounted for when a business plans its cash flow. Accurate payroll also gives management a more reliable picture of what the business actually spends on its people. Getting it right is a simple but important part of financial control. Managing Business Expenses and Financial Controls Financial

articles.summary: Alcon to Showcase Extensive Scientific Research, Immersive Experiences and Innovation at Academy 2026 sandra.hoffer Mon, 09/28/2026 - 14:56 Tuesday, September 29, 2026 New research will highlight patient satisfaction, symptom alleviation and quality of life across Alcon’s pharmaceutical and over-the-counter dry eye portfolio1-4 Latest science across Alcon WaterInnovations portfolio and lens care solutions will reinforce Alcon’s commitment to advancing healthy lens wear5,6 MARLO, the Alcon WaterInnovations Immersive Experience and the Innovation Suite to provide interactive learning experiences that help translate science into clinical practice FORT WORTH, Texas, September 29, 2026 — Alcon (SIX/NYSE: ALC), the global leader in eye care dedicated to helping people see brilliantly, today announced it will present new scientific research and offer a range of educational and immersive experiences at Academy 2026 (American Academy of Optometry Annual Meeting), taking place September 30–October 3 in Anaheim, California. Alcon will share research spanning dry eye disease, contact lenses and contact lens care, including new scientific presentations related to TRYPTYR® (acoltremon ophthalmic solution) 0.003% and the company’s broader dry eye portfolio. Attendees will also have opportunities to engage with Alcon innovations through the WaterInnovations™ Immersive Experience, MARLO demonstrations and an Innovation Suite featuring Voyager™ Direct Selective Laser Trabeculoplasty (DSLT) and the Valeda® photobiomodulation (PBM) device. “Academy 2026 provides an important opportunity for Alcon to advance scientific exchange around dry eye disease and deepen understanding of the patient experience,” said Lisa Praeger, General Manager, U.S. Ocular Health Pharmaceutical, Alcon. “Following the U.S. launch of TRYPTYR, our continued investment in research across our pharmaceutical and over-the-counter dry eye portfolio reflects Alcon’s commitment to supporting eye care professionals with evidence and education. We look forward to engaging with the optometric community around new research that can help inform conversations with patients and clinical practice.” Advancing Dry Eye Science and Scientific Exchange At Academy 2026, Alcon will present new dry eye research examining patient satisfaction, symptoms and quality of life across its pharmaceutical and over-the-counter dry eye portfolio.2,3 The research will explore a range of patient experiences and clinical considerations, including treatment satisfaction, the impact of dry eye on daily activities and work, patient-reported symptoms and measures of tear film and meibomian gland function. 2,3 Featured dry eye poster presentations include: Comparing Patient-Reported Symptoms in Perfluorohexyloctane Ophthalmic Solution and SYSTANE® PRO Users2 Assessing Meibomian Gland Function in Dry Eye Subjects Treated with PFHO or SYSTANE® PRO3 Nearly one year after the U.S. commercial launch of TRYPTYR, Academy will also feature new research focused on the experiences of people with dry eye disease treated with acoltremon ophthalmic solution 0.003%, including quality of life, daily functioning and treatment satisfaction.1,4 Featured TRYPTYR poster presentations include: Evaluating the Impact of Acoltremon 0.003% on a Subject’s Quality of Life and Ability to Perform Work4 Understanding the Satisfaction of Symptomatic Lifitegrast Patients Who Switched to Acoltremon1 Supporting Healthy Contact Lens Wear Through Research and Education Alcon will also present new research across its contact lens portfolio, with scientific presentations focused on lens performance, wearer experience and the evolving needs of patients and Eye Care Professionals.5,6 The research includes studies evaluating weekly replacement and daily disposable lenses, with a focus on factors such as vision, comfort, digital device use and patient satisfaction.5,6 Featured contact lens presentations include: Performance and Safety Evaluation of Weekly Replacement Serafilcon A Compared to Biweekly Replacement Senofilcon A Silicone Hydrogel Contact Lenses5 Evaluation of Wear Experience with a Weekly Replacement Toric Contact Lens in Neophyte Wearers6 Alcon will also host an educational luncheon focused on expanded toric parameters within the WaterInnovations portfolio, offering attendees an additional opportunity to engage with education related to contact lens fitting and patient needs. Bringing Science and Innovation to Life at Academy In addition to its scientific presentations, Alcon will offer educational and immersive experiences throughout Academy that give ECPs opportunities to explore new technologies, engage with Alcon experts and consider how innovations may support patient care and practice needs. The Alcon WaterInnovations Immersive Experience will bring the science behind the portfolio to life through an interactive educational environment, giving attendees an opportunity to explore the technologies and scientific principles supporting the WaterInnovations portfolio. The Innovation Suite will feature Voyager DSLT and Valeda PBM, giving optometrists an opportunity to learn more about technologies supporting care for patients with glaucoma and dry age-related macular degeneration (AMD).7-10 Attendees will also be able to explore MARLO through demonstrations in the Alcon booth, along with additional professional education and meeting activities designed to help Eye Care Professionals engage with Alcon innovations and scientific programming. For the full schedule of Alcon scientific presentations, educational programming, demonstrations and meeting activities, visit www.myalcon.com/professional/events/alcon-at-aoa . Attendees can also visit Alcon at booth #712. About Alcon Alcon helps people see brilliantly. As the global leader in eye care with a heritage spanning over 75 years, we offer the broadest portfolio of products to enhance sight and improve people’s lives. Our Surgical and Vision Care products touch the lives of more than 260 million people in over 140 countries and territories each year living with conditions like cataracts, glaucoma, retinal diseases and refractive errors. Our more than 25,000 associates are enhancing the quality of life through innovative products, partnerships with Eye Care Professionals and programs that advance access to quality eye care. Learn more at www.alcon.com . Connect with us on Facebook and LinkedIn . TRYPTYR INDICATIONS AND USAGE TRYPTYR (acoltremon ophthalmic solution) 0.003% is indicated for the treatment of the signs and symptoms of dry eye disease (DED). TRYPTYR IMPORTANT SAFETY INFORMATION Warnings and Precautions Potential for Eye Injury and Contamination: To avoid the potential for eye injury and contamination, advise patients not to touch the vial tip to the eye or other surfaces. Use with Contact Lenses: TRYPTYR should not be administered while wearing contact lenses. If contact lenses are worn, they should be removed prior to administration of the solution. Lenses may be reinserted 15 minutes following administration of TRYPTYR. Adverse Reactions In clinical trials, the most common adverse reaction was instillation site pain (50%). Please click here for the TRYPTYR Full Prescribing Information. About Valeda PBM Valeda PBM multiwavelength treatments are for patients suffering from dry AMD. The Food & Drug Administration (FDA) has authorized marketing of the PBM device treatment for dry AMD patients to improve vision. About Voyager DSLT Indications / Intended Use: The Direct Selective Laser Trabeculoplasty (DSLT) device is an ophthalmic laser device designed for performing selective laser trabeculoplasty. It is an automated device for direct selective laser trabeculoplasty (DSLT) that employs a Q‒switched, 3‒ns pulse width, frequency-doubled Nd: YAG laser of wavelength 532 nm. It directs the 400‒μm diameter laser beam to the eye limbus region without any contact with the patient's eye. An image-processing algorithm automatically locates the target area on the limbus, which the operator or Eye Care Professional (ECP) adjusts as necessary. After the operator confirms the limbus target, an eye-tracking algorithm tracks eye movement so that the laser pulses are delivered accurately to the targeted location on the limbus.
